findings.page: PDF p. 155 (printed p. 131); also PDF p. 144 (printed p. 120) and PDF p. 146 (printed p. 122)
findings.chapter: Ch. 6 — Measuring What Matters: From Telemetry to Architecture Decisions
findings.evidence: §6.1.1 (PDF p. 144): "Queue depth is not one of them: it is a scheduler state, a leading indicator that helps explain these serving metrics." Fig. 6.1 (PDF p. 146) carries the same box label: "queue depth: scheduler state, not a serving metric". But §6.3.4 (PDF p. 155) reads: "We see: p95 TTFT climbing (serving), KV cache hit ratio low (resource: FLOP/reuse — prefill recomputation), and prefill queue depth growing (serving)." And §6.4 (PDF p. 155): "Deploy counters at all three layers from day one — rps and token profile (workload); TTFT/TPOT/goodput percentiles and queue depth (serving — queue depth being the scheduler state that explains the others); HBM bandwidth, FLOP/MFU, KV cache occupancy, memory pressure (resource)."
findings.issue: Queue depth is given two mutually exclusive classifications inside one chapter. §6.1.1 and Fig. 6.1 explicitly exclude it from the serving-metric layer (it is scheduler state); §6.3.4 then tags it '(serving)' in the worked dashboard trace, and §6.4 lists it inside the serving group. The metric hierarchy is the book's diagnostic spine ('never jump from a workload metric straight to a serving metric'), and §6.3.4's trace is the chapter's demonstration of reading the chain upward — so a reader following the example would place a scheduler-state counter in the serving layer, contradicting the chapter's own taxonomy and its statement that queue depth is 'a leading indicator that helps explain these serving metrics' rather than one of them.
findings.fix_instruction: Pick one classification and apply it in all three places. Recommended: keep the §6.1.1/Fig. 6.1 taxonomy (queue depth = scheduler state, not a serving metric) and correct §6.3.4 to read 'prefill queue depth growing (scheduler state — a leading indicator of the serving symptom above)' and §6.4 to list queue depth as a separate scheduler-side counter rather than inside the serving group. If instead queue depth is to be reclassified as a serving metric, change §6.1.1 and the Fig. 6.1 box label accordingly and state the consequence for the causal chain.

findings.evidence: PDF p.145 (§6.1.1): "Queue depth is not one of them: it is a scheduler state, a leading indicator that helps explain these serving metrics." PDF p.146 (Fig 6.1 caption): "queue depth: scheduler state, not a serving metric". But PDF p.155 (§6.3.4): "...and prefill queue depth growing (serving)" and PDF p.156 (§6.4): "TTFT/TPOT/goodput percentiles and queue depth (serving — queue depth being the scheduler state that explains the others)".
findings.issue: Layer-classification drift for queue depth: §6.1.1 and the Fig 6.1 caption explicitly exclude queue depth from the serving-metric layer, while §6.3.4 tags queue depth with a bare "(serving)" layer label and §6.4 groups it under the serving-layer instrumentation bullet. The same quantity carries two conflicting layer classifications within one chapter.
findings.fix_instruction: Retag "prefill queue depth growing (serving)" in §6.3.4 as "(scheduler state)" or "(serving-adjacent scheduler state)"; in §6.4 either move queue depth out of the serving bullet into its own clause ("plus queue depth — a scheduler state that explains the serving metrics") or add a parenthetical noting it is instrumented alongside serving metrics but classified per §6.1.1. Sweep Ch. 6 (and Ch. 20's fleet metrics, if queue depth reappears) for other bare layer tags on queue depth.
